title: You 2.0: How to Break Out of a Rut

sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: There are moments in any journey when things can feel interminable.
sentences.zh: 在任何旅程中，总会有那么一些时刻，你会觉得一切都漫长得没有尽头。

sentences.en: You show up to work every day, do the same job, meet the same people.
sentences.zh: 你每天去上班，做同样的工作，见同样的人。

sentences.en: At home, you wash the dishes, clean the bedroom, do the laundry.
sentences.zh: 在家里，你洗碗、打扫卧室、洗衣服。

sentences.en: On weekends, you watch the same TV shows, go for the same walks, talk to the same relatives.
sentences.zh: 周末，你看同样的电视节目，去同样的地方散步，和同样的亲戚聊天。

sentences.en: One day starts to look like the next.
sentences.zh: 每一天看起来都和前一天没什么两样。
几周的时间模糊地交织在一起。

sentences.en: And then you start to wonder, what am I really doing?
sentences.zh: 然后你开始怀疑，我到底在做什么？

sentences.en: Am I making any progress at all?
sentences.zh: 我真的有取得任何进展吗？

sentences.en: We have different names for this phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 我们对这种现象有不同的称呼。
作家说他们遇到了瓶颈。

sentences.en: Office workers talk about being in a rut.
sentences.zh: 上班族说他们陷入了死循环。

sentences.en: People of a certain age call it a midlife crisis.
sentences.zh: 到了特定年纪的人称之为中年危机。

sentences.en: But they are all different ways of saying, I'm stuck.
sentences.zh: 但这些其实都是在表达同一种意思：我卡住了。

sentences.en: Today, we begin our perennially popular annual series, U2.0.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们开启备受欢迎的年度系列节目《U2.0》。

sentences.en: In past years, we have explored ideas about how to communicate better or build stronger relationships.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，我们探讨过如何更好地沟通或建立更稳固的关系。

sentences.en: In the coming weeks, we will explore a variety of new ideas to help you thrive.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几周里，我们将探索各种新思路，帮助你实现蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, new research into the science of feeling stuck and powerful insights into how to get unstuck.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》将深入研究“卡住”这种感觉的科学，并提供关于如何摆脱困境的深刻见解。

sentences.en: All of us have had moments in our lives when we feel stuck.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人在生活中都曾有过感到卡住的时刻。

sentences.en: We don't know what we want to do.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道自己想做什么。

sentences.en: Or if we do know what we want, we don't know how to do it.
sentences.zh: 或者即使知道自己想要什么，也不知道该如何实现。

sentences.en: At New York University, psychologist Adam Alter studies the science of how to get unstuck.
sentences.zh: 在纽约大学，心理学家亚当·奥尔特专门研究如何摆脱困境的科学。

sentences.en: Adam Alter, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 亚当·奥尔特，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Adam, I want to play you a clip from a very dramatic and popular TV series.
sentences.zh: 亚当，我想给你播放一段非常戏剧化且热门的电视剧片段。

sentences.en: This is from the Season 7 trailer of Game of Thrones.
sentences.zh: 这是《权力的游戏》第七季的预告片。

sentences.en: For centuries, our families fought together against their common enemy, despite their differences together.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，我们的家族尽管存在分歧，但始终并肩对抗共同的敌人。

sentences.en: We need to do the same if we're going to survive, because the enemy is real, always been real.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想生存下去，就必须继续这样做，因为敌人是真实存在的，一直都是。

sentences.en: Now, Adam, you've spent some time thinking about this, because even as the TV show is wildly dramatic and packed with action,
sentences.zh: 现在，亚当，你花了一些时间思考这个问题，因为尽管这部电视剧极其戏剧化且充满动作场面，

sentences.en: something very curious was happening to the writer of the series.
sentences.zh: 但该剧的作者身上却发生了一件非常奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: Martin started writing this epic fantasy and what happened along the way.
sentences.zh: 马丁是如何开始创作这部史诗奇幻作品的，以及在此过程中发生了什么。

sentences.en: He wrote a number of books in the series, and the gap between those books grew larger and larger
sentences.zh: 他写了这个系列中的好几本书，而这些书之间的间隔变得越来越长，

sentences.en: to the point where he experienced what he described as profound writer's block.
sentences.zh: 以至于他经历了自己所描述的严重的写作瓶颈。

sentences.en: And he's expressed great puzzlement because he was so productive for so long, but now says in interviews,
sentences.zh: 他对此感到非常困惑，因为他长期以来一直非常高产，但现在他在采访中说，

sentences.en: I don't really have an explanation for you.
sentences.zh: 我真的无法给你一个解释。

sentences.en: I know you as the fans of the series are looking for the next installment.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们作为该系列的粉丝，都在期待下一部的出版。

sentences.en: I just don't know what to say.
sentences.zh: 我只是不知道该说什么。

sentences.en: I just haven't been able to produce it.
sentences.zh: 我就是没能把它写出来。

sentences.en: And that's where we sit now.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们目前的处境。

sentences.en: So fans of the books are waiting for the next installment to be released, even as the TV show itself has been completed.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管电视剧本身已经完结，但书迷们仍在等待下一部的出版。

sentences.en: In an interview in 2018, he said,
sentences.zh: 在2018年的一次采访中，他说，

sentences.en: I know there are a lot of people out there who are very angry with me that Winds of Winter,
sentences.zh: 我知道外面有很多人对我非常生气，因为《凛冬的寒风》，

sentences.en: this is the sixth volume out of seven, isn't finished.
sentences.zh: 也就是七卷中的第六卷，还没有完成。

sentences.en: And I'm mad about that myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己也为此感到恼火。

sentences.en: I wish I finished it four years ago.
sentences.zh: 我希望我四年前就写完了。

sentences.en: I wish it was finished now, but it's not.
sentences.zh: 我希望它现在已经完成了，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: But I've had dark nights of the soul where I've pounded my head against the keyboard and said,
sentences.zh: 但我经历过灵魂的至暗时刻，我曾对着键盘捶头，自问：

sentences.en: God, will I ever finish this?
The show is going further and further forward.
sentences.zh: 剧集正在不断向前推进。

sentences.en: He's talking here about Game of Thrones.
sentences.zh: 他这里指的是《权力的游戏》。

sentences.en: And I'm falling further and further behind.
sentences.zh: 而我却被甩得越来越远。

sentences.en: What the hell is happening here?
And you can almost hear his own mystification about his own block here, Adam.
sentences.zh: 亚当，你几乎可以从他的话语中听到他对自身瓶颈的困惑。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's interesting when you see someone who is such a colossal talent for writing these kinds of stories.
sentences.zh: 是的，当你看到一个在创作这类故事方面拥有如此巨大天赋的人时，这确实很有趣。

sentences.en: And yet still, we're not talking about being stuck for a day or a week or a month.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们谈论的并不是卡住一天、一周或一个月。

sentences.en: We're talking about a matter of many years.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是长达数年的时间。

sentences.en: And he has no idea what he's supposed to be doing moving forward.
sentences.zh: 而且他完全不知道接下来该怎么做。

sentences.en: So it's a very profound case of stuckness.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常严重的卡住案例。

sentences.en: So you say that George R.R.
Martin and people like him might have something to learn from an experiment conducted many years ago by the psychologist Clark Hull.
sentences.zh: 马丁和像他这样的人，或许可以从心理学家克拉克·赫尔多年前进行的一项实验中学到一些东西。

sentences.en: What makes this experiment unusual is that the test subjects were mice?
sentences.zh: 这个实验的不同寻常之处在于，测试对象是老鼠？

sentences.en: Hull was a behaviorist and a lot of behaviorists in that period in the middle of the 20th century studied mice because they were very easy to study.
sentences.zh: 赫尔是一位行为主义者，20世纪中叶那个时期的许多行为主义者都研究老鼠，因为它们非常容易研究。

sentences.en: They were very interested in some very basic psychological principles that applied to mice just as they did to humans.
sentences.zh: 他们对一些适用于老鼠也同样适用于人类的基本心理学原理非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And so Hull used to create mazes for his mice and he would watch as they completed these mazes.
sentences.zh: 因此，赫尔过去常为他的老鼠制作迷宫，并观察它们完成这些迷宫的过程。

sentences.en: What do mice running through a maze have to do with a writer of epic fantasy novels getting stuck?
sentences.zh: 老鼠跑迷宫和史诗奇幻小说作家遇到瓶颈有什么关系？

sentences.en: The thing that he noticed most was that the mice, when they first entered the maze, were quite slow to move.
sentences.zh: 他注意到最重要的一点是，老鼠在刚进入迷宫时，移动速度相当慢。

sentences.en: They were puzzled by the situation that faced them.
sentences.zh: 它们对眼前的处境感到困惑。

sentences.en: But as the goal, whatever the goal was, whether it was a piece of food or whether it was exiting the maze, as the goal came into view, they moved much more quickly.
sentences.zh: 但随着目标——无论是食物还是迷宫出口——进入视野，它们移动的速度就快多了。

sentences.en: And he described this as the goal gradient.
sentences.zh: 他将其描述为“目标梯度”。

sentences.en: It's the idea that, at least subjectively, it feels to mice and actually to humans as well,
sentences.zh: 这个概念是说，至少在主观上，对于老鼠甚至人类来说，

sentences.en: as though, as you can see the goal in sight, that the experience becomes almost metaphorically downhill.
sentences.zh: 当你能看到目标时，那种体验在隐喻上就像是在下坡。

sentences.en: It's much easier to bridge the gap between where you are and where you'd like to be.
sentences.zh: 弥合你当前位置与你想去的地方之间的差距会变得容易得多。

sentences.en: And I think all of us have had this experience in one form or the other.
sentences.zh: 我想我们所有人都以这样或那样的形式经历过这种体验。

sentences.en: You know, you feel like the end is in sight, whether you're a runner and you can see the finish tape inside.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你觉得终点在望时，无论你是一名跑步者并能看到终点线，

sentences.en: It does give you a bit of a spurt to get to the finish line.
sentences.zh: 这确实会给你一点冲刺到终点的动力。

sentences.en: But talk a minute about this goal gradient idea, because there's something really interesting that happens here at the start, the middle, and at the end.
sentences.zh: 但请谈谈这个“目标梯度”的概念，因为在起点、中间和终点发生的事情确实非常有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the original idea that Hal described was that we're much quicker, closer to the goal.
sentences.zh: 是的，赫尔描述的最初想法是，我们离目标越近，速度就越快。

sentences.en: But subsequent research has shown that it's a bit more complicated than that, that actually we slow down dramatically in the middle when we're sort of unmoored.
sentences.zh: 但随后的研究表明情况要复杂一些，实际上我们在中间阶段会明显慢下来，因为那时我们处于一种“无锚”状态。

sentences.en: We're somewhere between the beginning of the goal and the end of the goal.
sentences.zh: 我们处于目标起点和终点之间的某个位置。

sentences.en: And so we move quickly at the beginning because we have a bit of motivation, we're fresh, we're ready to go, and we slow down in the middle.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在开始时移动得很快，因为我们有一点动力，我们精力充沛，准备出发，然后在中间阶段慢了下来。

sentences.en: And then as we get to the end of the process, we speed up again as the goal comes within view.
sentences.zh: 然后当我们接近过程的终点时，随着目标进入视野，我们又加快了速度。

sentences.en: So it's a sort of U-shape.
You go quickly, then slowly, then quickly again.
sentences.zh: 你先快，然后慢，最后又快起来。

sentences.en: Adam says it is revealing that George R.R.
Martin got stuck as he was slogging his way through the series.
sentences.zh: 马丁在创作该系列的过程中步履维艰，这很能说明问题。

sentences.en: The end of the series was some distance away, while the start of the project was in the distant paSt.
sentences.zh: 系列终点还很遥远，而项目的起点已在遥远的过去。

sentences.en: There's lots of evidence that the goal gradient effect plays a powerful role in many dimensions of our lives.
sentences.zh: 有大量证据表明，目标梯度效应在我们生活的许多方面都发挥着强大的作用。

sentences.en: There are some studies that show that it applies to physical activity, but it applies just as much to mental activity as well.
sentences.zh: 有一些研究表明它适用于体育活动，但也同样适用于脑力活动。

sentences.en: So there were some studies that were run asking people, for example, one of my colleagues, Andrea Bonetzi, and his colleagues asked people to find words within words.
sentences.zh: 有一些研究是这样进行的，比如我的同事安德里亚·博内齐和他的同事要求人们在词语中寻找词语。

sentences.en: So he would give them a long word, and then he would say, how many shorter English words can you find within the letters of this longer word?
sentences.zh: 他会给他们一个长单词，然后问，你能在这些长单词的字母中找到多少个较短的英语单词？

sentences.en: And he did that nine times.
And what he found was that people were slowest around the fifth attempt, much slower than around the first or second or eighth or ninth attempts.
sentences.zh: 他发现人们在第五次尝试时最慢，比第一次、第二次、第八次或第九次尝试时慢得多。

sentences.en: And so this applies just as much in his studies to mental activities where there's some motivation required as it does to physical activities.
sentences.zh: 因此，在他的研究中，这同样适用于需要一定动力的脑力活动，就像适用于体育活动一样。

sentences.en: I understand this is also true when it comes to paying off credit card debt.
sentences.zh: 我明白这在偿还信用卡债务时也适用。

sentences.en: You know, you make a good start at the beginning, and if you get close to the end, you feel like you have a sport to finish off.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在开始时做得很好，如果你接近尾声，你会觉得有动力去完成它。

sentences.en: But the middle is really difficult again.
sentences.zh: 但中间阶段确实又变得非常困难。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's quite a lot of research on the financial implications of this stuck-in-the-middle effect, as it's known, that shows exactly that,
sentences.zh: 是的，关于这种所谓的“中间卡住效应”的财务影响，有很多研究表明了这一点，

sentences.en: that we pay off credit card debt quickly, then slowly, then quickly.
sentences.zh: 我们偿还信用卡债务时是先快，再慢，最后又快。

sentences.en: When we're donating to charities, you see something similar.
sentences.zh: 当我们向慈善机构捐款时，也会看到类似的情况。

sentences.en: We donate much more readily, and we donate larger amounts at the beginning when the charity first makes the solicitation.
sentences.zh: 在慈善机构最初发出募捐请求时，我们更乐意捐款，捐款金额也更大。

sentences.en: And then again, as the charity reaches its goal or approaches its goal, we donate again.
sentences.zh: 然后，当慈善机构达到或接近其目标时，我们又会再次捐款。

sentences.en: But in the middle process, say the charity is looking for $100,000, around that $50,000 mark, you see a slowdown collectively in how much people give.
sentences.zh: 但在中间过程中，假设慈善机构的目标是10万美元，在5万美元左右时，你会看到人们的捐款速度整体放缓。

sentences.en: So you argue that one of the reasons that the middle of a project is so challenging is that there are fewer and fewer landmarks to mark our progress.
sentences.zh: 所以你认为项目中间阶段之所以如此具有挑战性，原因之一是标记我们进展的里程碑越来越少了。

sentences.en: And you've compared the journey we take on a long project to the experience of a sailor on a ship traveling across the Atlantic Ocean from the United States to Britain.
sentences.zh: 你把我们在长期项目中的旅程比作水手横渡大西洋从美国前往英国的经历。
解释一下这个类比，亚当。

sentences.en: Yeah, so when you leave, imagine you're sailing from New York to, say, Southampton in Britain.
sentences.zh: 是的，当你离开时，想象一下你正从纽约航行到英国的南安普敦。

sentences.en: When you leave, you have a number of landmarks behind you, and there's a lot of activity at the beginning of that journey, things that suggest that you're moving.
sentences.zh: 当你离开时，身后有许多地标，旅程开始时有很多活动，这些都表明你正在前进。

sentences.en: You can see how fast you're moving.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到你的移动速度有多快。

sentences.en: And when you get into the middle part of that journey, all you see is ocean.
sentences.zh: 当你进入旅程的中段时，你看到的只有海洋。

sentences.en: But you don't have any external cues that tell you how fast you're moving.
sentences.zh: 你没有任何外部线索来告诉你移动得有多快。

sentences.en: And so that middle period is a long period between leaving the land behind and then waiting for the next bit of land to come into view.
sentences.zh: 所以中间那段时期是离开陆地后到等待下一片陆地进入视野之间的漫长时期。

sentences.en: And so during that period, in contrast to the beginning of the experience, you don't have a lot of feedback about your progress.
sentences.zh: 因此在那段时间里，与体验的开始阶段相比，你没有太多关于进展的反馈。

sentences.en: You know, it gives you the sense that you're not really making progress, even if you're moving quite rapidly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这会让你觉得即使你移动得很快，也没有真正取得进展。

sentences.en: And then, of course, as you approach Britain again, you see land.
sentences.zh: 当然，当你再次接近英国时，你会看到陆地。

sentences.en: You might see parts of the British Isles.
sentences.zh: 你可能会看到不列颠群岛的部分地区。

sentences.en: And again, you can start to see how fast you're moving.
sentences.zh: 同样，你可以开始看到你的移动速度有多快。

sentences.en: You're getting some external cues that are reinforcing.
sentences.zh: 你得到了一些能起到强化作用的外部线索。

sentences.en: And I think that's how a lot of our goals function.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是我们许多目标运作的方式。

sentences.en: We have that middle period that can often be quite expansive, where we just have no sense that we're making progress.
sentences.zh: 我们有那段往往非常漫长的中间时期，在那里我们根本感觉不到自己在取得进展。

sentences.en: So is one solution then to try and create more landmarks in the middle?
sentences.zh: 那么，一个解决方案是尝试在中间阶段创造更多的里程碑吗？

sentences.en: I think it's to shrink the middles as far as possible.
sentences.zh: 我认为是要尽可能缩短中间阶段。

sentences.en: And there are different ways to do that.
sentences.zh: 有不同的方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: In the case of sailing, there aren't that many options.
sentences.zh: 在航海的情况下，选择并不多。

sentences.en: But what you want to do is to give yourself some sort of feedback that suggests that you're making progress.
sentences.zh: 但你想做的是给自己提供某种反馈，表明你正在取得进展。

sentences.en: And so you might create sub-goals.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以设定子目标。

sentences.en: Instead of thinking of the journey as a single goal from start to finish, you might say,
sentences.zh: 与其把旅程看作是从起点到终点的单一目标，你不如说，

sentences.en: well, you know, I've got this map that I'm using to navigate through the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我有一张用来在大西洋航行的地图。

sentences.en: I know when I hit certain latitude or longitudinal measures, I know that I've reached a certain percentage of the way.
sentences.zh: 我知道当我到达某些纬度或经度时，我就完成了某一部分的航程。

sentences.en: And that's obviously much easier to do when you're engaged in some sort of activity,
sentences.zh: 当你从事某种活动时，这显然要容易得多，

sentences.en: whether it's running or whether it's some sort of mental activity.
sentences.zh: 无论是跑步还是某种脑力活动。

sentences.en: You just kind of shrink the goal down.
You bracket it much more narrowly.
sentences.zh: 你把它的范围界定得更窄。

sentences.en: So you have these smaller sub-goals.
sentences.zh: 所以你有了这些更小的子目标。

sentences.en: So runners often say, you know, my goal is to run the next mile or the next half mile.
sentences.zh: 跑步者经常说，我的目标是跑完下一英里或半英里。

sentences.en: Or even, you know, as far as my eye can see.
sentences.zh: 甚至，你知道，只要我视线所及的地方。

sentences.en: And you set a target and you run to that target.
sentences.zh: 你设定一个目标，然后向那个目标跑去。

sentences.en: And then you look at another target and you run to that target.
sentences.zh: 然后你再看向下一个目标，并向那个目标跑去。
